new_findings.finding: rotateDeviceKey and first-key creation are not serialized across extension contexts. Two callers can read K0, each prepare a pending candidate, then write KA and KB. If KA becomes active long enough to sign a receipt before KB overwrites it, the final history still marks KA pending; getPublicKeyById filters it because KB is active, so that receipt becomes unverifiable. The Settings button's local busy state does not serialize separate side-panel instances or other contexts.
new_findings.evidence: src/lib/audit/device-key.ts:168-177, 210-220, 223-253, 279-307; pending entries are only exposed while matching the current active key. No shared lock, compare-and-swap, or post-write lineage reconciliation is present.
new_findings.required_resolution: Make key creation/rotation a single-writer operation across extension contexts or reconcile every key that could have become active into durable history before hiding it. Add a forced interleaving test where two writers overlap and the first key signs before the second commit; verify both receipts after restart.

verdict_b_quality.test_quality: Focused tests assert real WebCrypto signatures against isolated storage and exercise the primitive boundary, but only sequential writer cases are covered; they do not establish cross-context serialization or concurrent lineage safety.
